meditations.8.6.you: When facing a big change, list how it resembles changes you've already survived.

meditations.8.7.meaning: Every nature is content when it goes well. A rational nature goes well when it agrees to nothing false or uncertain, aims its actions at the common good, desires and avoids only what's in its power, and welcomes what nature assigns.
meditations.8.7.today: Four practical tests of a mind working well: truth, service, focus and acceptance.
meditations.8.7.you: Score your week on the four: did I avoid false beliefs, act for others, focus on what I control, accept what came?

meditations.8.8.meaning: You don't have time to read? But you do have time to check arrogance, rise above pleasure and pain, rise above love of fame, and not be annoyed at stupid, ungrateful people, even to care for them.
meditations.8.8.today: Busy people can't always study, but they can always practise character.
meditations.8.8.you: On days with no time for reading, pick one of these practices to do instead.

meditations.8.9.meaning: Let no one hear you complaining about life at court, or about your own life, any more.
meditations.8.9.today: Complaining is a habit that spreads and sours. Stopping it changes how we feel.
meditations.8.9.you: Try a week without complaining about work or home, out loud or online. See what happens.

meditations.8.10.meaning: Regret is self-reproach for neglecting something useful. A good person would never regret passing up a sensual pleasure, so pleasure isn't good or useful.
meditations.8.10.today: We rarely regret skipping indulgence. That tells us something about its value.
meditations.8.10.you: Next time you're tempted by an indulgence, ask whether you'd regret skipping it. Usually not.

meditations.8.11.meaning: What is this thing in itself? What's it made of? What's its form? What's it doing in the world? How long will it last?
meditations.8.11.today: Five analytic questions that cut through hype and emotion.
meditations.8.11.you: Apply the five questions to a new tool, opportunity or worry before you commit to it.

meditations.8.12.meaning: When you get up reluctantly, remember that social action is what human nature is for, while sleep is shared with animals. What's specific to your nature is more your own, and more satisfying.
meditations.8.12.today: Another morning pep talk: rising to serve is more human, and more rewarding, than staying in bed.
meditations.8.12.you: Tomorrow morning, tie getting up to someone you'll help today, at work or at home.

meditations.8.13.meaning: Constantly, and if possible with every impression, apply the principles of physics, ethics and logic.
meditations.8.13.today: Understand how things work, what's right, and whether your reasoning holds. It's a full-stack approach to thinking.
meditations.8.13.you: In your next big decision, check all three: the facts, the ethics and the logic.

meditations.8.14.meaning: Whoever you meet, ask yourself what they believe about good and bad. Knowing their beliefs about pleasure, pain, fame and death, you won't be surprised by what they do; they're compelled by those beliefs.
meditations.8.14.today: Understanding people's values predicts their behaviour and defuses frustration.
meditations.8.14.you: Before a negotiation, map the other side's beliefs about what's good. Their moves will make more sense.

meditations.8.15.meaning: It's shameful to be surprised that a fig tree bears figs, and equally shameful to be surprised when the world produces what it produces. Doctors aren't surprised by fever, nor sailors by contrary winds.
meditations.8.15.today: Professionals expect the predictable problems of their field. We should expect life's too.
meditations.8.15.you: You wouldn't be surprised by a bug in new code. Don't be surprised by friction in a new team either.

meditations.8.17.meaning: If it's up to you, why do it? If it's up to someone else, who will you blame? Blame no one. If you can, fix the cause. If not, fix the thing. If not even that, what's the use of complaining?
meditations.8.17.today: A tidy flowchart for frustration: fix the cause, fix the symptom, or let it go.
meditations.8.17.you: Run your current frustration through the flowchart. Which step applies?

meditations.8.18.meaning: What dies doesn't fall out of the universe. It stays and changes into its elements, which are elements of the universe and of you. And they don't complain about it.
meditations.8.18.today: It pictures death as recycling within a closed system, where nothing is lost, only changed.
meditations.8.18.you: Let it soften fear of endings: nothing leaves the system; it transforms.

meditations.8.19.meaning: Everything exists for a purpose: a horse, a vine, even the sun. What's your purpose? Pleasure? See if common sense accepts that.
meditations.8.19.today: A clear sense of purpose is linked to wellbeing and resilience. Pleasure alone rarely satisfies.
meditations.8.19.you: Write your purpose in one sentence. If it's about pleasure or comfort, try again.

meditations.8.20.meaning: Nature cares about the end as much as the beginning, like someone throwing a ball. What good is it to the ball to go up, or harm to come down? Or to a bubble to hold together, or to burst?
meditations.8.20.today: Rising and falling are both part of the arc. Neither is a tragedy.
meditations.8.20.you: Whatever phase you're in, career rising or plateauing, remember the ball: both halves belong to the throw.

meditations.8.21.meaning: Turn the body inside out and see what it is, and what it becomes in age and illness. Praiser and praised, rememberer and remembered are short-lived, in one small corner of the earth, and even there no one agrees.
meditations.8.21.today: It deflates both vanity about looks and the desire for praise.
meditations.8.21.you: When image or reputation weighs on you, recall how small and short-lived both are.

meditations.8.23.meaning: Am I doing something? I do it for the good of people. Does something happen to me? I accept it and refer it to the source of all things.
meditations.8.23.today: Two orientations: act for others, accept what comes. It covers most of life.
meditations.8.23.you: Use it as a two-line daily frame: act for others, accept what comes.

meditations.8.24.meaning: Bathing looks like oil, sweat, dirt and filthy water, all disgusting. So is every part of life and everything in it.
meditations.8.24.today: A deliberately unglamorous view, useful for puncturing obsession with appearances.
meditations.8.24.you: When something looks glamorous, look at its bathwater: the unglamorous reality behind it.

meditations.8.25.meaning: Lucilla saw Verus die, then died. Secunda saw Maximus die, then died. Antoninus saw Faustina die, then died. The clever and proud, all gone. That's everything.
meditations.8.25.today: A roll-call of the dead, including Marcus's own family, makes mortality personal.
meditations.8.25.you: Think of the generations before you in your own family. Then ask how you want to spend your turn.

meditations.8.26.meaning: It's satisfying to do a human being's work: to be kind to your own kind, to disregard the senses' tugs, to judge appearances rightly, and to study nature and events.
meditations.8.26.today: Kindness, self-control, clear judgement and curiosity are the core human job description.
meditations.8.26.you: Which of the four gets least time in your week? Give it one deliberate slot.

meditations.8.27.meaning: You have three relationships: with your body, with the divine source of everything, and with the people you live with.
meditations.8.27.today: Health, meaning and relationships: three domains that need tending.
meditations.8.27.you: Check all three this week: body, sense of purpose, and the people at home.

meditations.8.28.meaning: Pain is bad either for the body, which can speak for itself, or for the soul, which can keep its calm by not judging pain as bad. Every judgement and desire is within, and no evil reaches that high.
meditations.8.28.today: Physical pain and mental suffering can be separated. The second is partly optional.
meditations.8.28.you: When you're unwell or sore, let the body feel it without letting the mind add suffering.

meditations.8.29.meaning: Wipe out your imaginings by telling yourself: it's in my power to keep this soul free of badness, desire and disturbance, to see each thing as it is and use it according to its value.
meditations.8.29.today: A self-talk script for regaining control of an agitated mind.
meditations.8.29.you: Memorise a short version for stressful moments: I can keep my mind clear and see this as it is.

meditations.8.30.meaning: Speak appropriately in the Senate and to everyone else, without affectation. Use plain speech.
meditations.8.30.today: Plain language builds trust. Jargon and performance erode it.
meditations.8.30.you: In your next presentation or email, cut the jargon. Say it plainly.

meditations.8.31.meaning: Augustus's whole court, family, friends and advisers are dead. Think of whole families dying out, tombstones reading the last of his race, all their efforts to leave heirs.
meditations.8.31.today: Dynasties end and family names die out. Building a legacy is far more fragile than it feels.
meditations.8.31.you: Invest in the people in front of you rather than an imagined legacy.

meditations.8.33.meaning: Receive wealth or success without arrogance, and be ready to let it go.
meditations.8.33.today: Humility in success and readiness to lose it are marks of steady character.
meditations.8.33.you: When things go well, stay humble. Picture losing it, and notice whether you'd be okay.

meditations.8.34.meaning: A person who resents events or cuts themselves off from others is like a severed hand. But nature allows us to rejoin the body, something given to no other part. Use that gift.
meditations.8.34.today: Isolation and resentment cut us off, but reconnection is always possible.
meditations.8.34.you: Is there someone you've cut off, at work or in the family? Nature lets you reattach. Reach out.

meditations.8.35.meaning: Just as nature turns every obstacle to its own use, a rational being can make every hindrance its material and use it for its purposes.
meditations.8.35.today: Another statement of the obstacle-as-way idea: resistance can be raw material.
meditations.8.35.you: Treat the week's biggest obstacle as material for something you're building.

meditations.8.37.meaning: Do Hadrian's favourites still sit by his tomb? Ridiculous. And if they did, would he know, or be pleased, or become immortal? They too aged and died.
meditations.8.37.today: Posthumous loyalty and remembrance don't benefit the dead. Care now.
meditations.8.37.you: Show care to people while they're alive to feel it.

meditations.8.38.meaning: If you can see sharply, look, and judge wisely, as the philosopher says.
meditations.8.38.today: Clear sight is a responsibility: use it to judge well.
meditations.8.38.you: You're trained to see systems clearly. Apply the same sharp sight to people and to yourself.

meditations.8.39.meaning: In a rational being, I see no virtue opposed to justice. But I see one opposed to love of pleasure: self-control.
meditations.8.39.today: Justice has no rival virtue; pleasure does. Temperance is its check.
meditations.8.39.you: Where does pleasure most often pull you off course? Make self-control your focus there.

meditations.8.40.meaning: Take away your opinion about what seems painful and you're safe. Who is this you? Reason. But I'm not only reason. Fine: let reason not trouble itself, and let the other parts speak for themselves.
meditations.8.40.today: Separating the reasoning self from bodily reactions gives the mind stable ground.
meditations.8.40.you: When stress hits, let your reasoning self stay calm even while the rest of you reacts.

meditations.8.41.meaning: Blocking the senses or desires harms an animal; blocking intelligence harms a thinking being. If pain or pleasure touches you, let the senses deal with it. But nothing blocks the mind unless it blocks itself.
meditations.8.41.today: External obstacles hit our plans, not our judgement. The mind is only stopped by itself.
meditations.8.41.you: When you feel stuck, ask whether the block is outside, or in how you're thinking about it.

meditations.8.42.meaning: It isn't right that I should hurt myself, when I've never deliberately hurt anyone else.
meditations.8.42.today: Self-compassion: treat yourself at least as kindly as you treat others.
meditations.8.42.you: Notice harsh self-talk this week and speak to yourself as you would to a colleague.

meditations.8.43.meaning: Different things delight different people. My delight is keeping my mind sound, not turning away from anyone or anything, welcoming all and using each according to its value.
meditations.8.43.today: A calm, open mind can be a source of joy in itself.
meditations.8.43.you: Find joy this week in simply meeting everything well, people and events alike.

meditations.8.45.meaning: Throw me wherever you like; I'll keep my inner self calm and content there. Is a change of place reason for my soul to be miserable, shrunken or frightened? Nothing is.
meditations.8.45.today: Moves, reorganisations and new roles needn't disturb inner stability.
meditations.8.45.you: If you're facing a change of role, location or team, carry your inner calm with you.

meditations.8.46.meaning: Nothing can happen to a person that isn't a human event, to an ox that isn't ox-like, to a vine that isn't vine-like. If what happens is normal and natural, why complain? Nature brings nothing you can't bear.
meditations.8.46.today: Our troubles are human-shaped, and humans have borne them before.
meditations.8.46.you: Whatever you're facing is a human trouble. Others have borne it; so can you.

meditations.8.51.meaning: Don't be sluggish in action, muddled in speech, wandering in thought, torn inside or gushing outside, or too busy for leisure. Even if people kill or curse you, your mind can stay pure like a clear spring, however much dirt is thrown in.
meditations.8.51.today: Balance and purity of mind: steady action, clear speech, inner calm, and time to rest.
meditations.8.51.you: Which of the six faults is most present in your week? And are you too busy for leisure?

meditations.8.52.meaning: Not knowing what the world is, you don't know where you are; not knowing its purpose, you don't know who you are. Why seek or avoid the praise of people who don't know where or who they are?
meditations.8.52.today: The applause of the confused isn't worth much.
meditations.8.52.you: Before chasing someone's praise, ask whether they understand the world and themselves.

meditations.8.53.meaning: Do you want praise from someone who curses himself three times an hour? To please someone who doesn't please himself? Who regrets nearly everything he does?
meditations.8.53.today: Seeking approval from unhappy, self-critical people is a losing game.
meditations.8.53.you: If you're chasing approval from someone chronically dissatisfied, stop. You'll never satisfy them.

meditations.8.54.meaning: Don't just breathe in harmony with the air around you; let your mind be in harmony with the intelligence that holds everything together.
meditations.8.54.today: As we breathe the same air, we can align our thinking with shared reason.
meditations.8.54.you: In a moment of calm this week, breathe slowly and align your thinking with what's reasonable and shared.

meditations.8.55.meaning: Wickedness doesn't harm the universe, and one person's wickedness doesn't harm another. It only harms the one who has it, who can be free of it whenever they choose.
meditations.8.55.today: Others' bad character is their burden, not yours.
meditations.8.55.you: When someone behaves badly towards you, remember their badness mainly harms them.

meditations.8.56.meaning: My neighbour's free will is as external to mine as their breath and body. We're made for each other, but each mind has its own domain, or my neighbour's badness would be my harm, and God didn't want my happiness to depend on someone else.
meditations.8.56.today: Healthy boundaries: we care for others, but our wellbeing isn't hostage to their choices.
meditations.8.56.you: Draw this boundary with a difficult person this week: care about them, but don't let their choices set your mood.

meditations.8.57.meaning: The sun's light spreads everywhere without being used up, travelling in straight lines and resting on whatever it meets. The mind should do the same: spread without draining, rest on things without force, and light what receives it.
meditations.8.57.today: Influence works best like light: steady, direct and gentle.
meditations.8.57.you: Lead like sunlight: steady and clear, not forcing, lighting up those who are open to it.

meditations.8.58.meaning: If you fear death, you fear either losing sensation or getting a different kind. With no sensation, you'll feel no harm. With a different kind, you'll be a different living thing and won't stop living.
meditations.8.58.today: Epicurus's logic against death anxiety, adopted by Marcus.
meditations.8.58.you: If fear of death visits, walk through the two options. Neither involves suffering.

meditations.8.60.meaning: An arrow moves one way, the mind another. Even when the mind is being careful or investigating, it still moves straight towards its target.
meditations.8.60.today: Deliberation isn't wandering. Careful thinking still makes progress.
meditations.8.60.you: When you're taking time to think a decision through, don't mistake it for indecision. It's aiming.

meditations.8.61.meaning: Get inside every person's mind, and let every other person get inside yours.
meditations.8.61.today: It asks for mutual understanding and transparency, running both ways between people.
meditations.8.61.you: Try to understand your colleagues deeply, and let them understand you: explain your reasoning more openly.

meditations.9.1.meaning: Injustice is impiety, because nature made rational beings to help each other, not harm each other. Lying is impiety too, since nature is truth. So is chasing pleasure as good and fleeing pain as evil, because nature treats them evenly and so should we.
meditations.9.1.today: Marcus ties honesty, fairness and equanimity together as one duty to reality itself, not just rules.
meditations.9.1.you: Treat honesty in your reporting and fairness in your decisions as a duty to reality, not just policy compliance.

meditations.9.2.meaning: The best fate would be to leave life never having tasted lying, hypocrisy, luxury or pride. Failing that, leave once you've had enough of them. Have you chosen to live with vice? Corruption of the mind is a worse plague than any disease in the air.
meditations.9.2.today: Moral corruption spreads like a disease, and it does more damage than illness.
meditations.9.2.you: Watch for small hypocrisies or luxuries creeping into your life, and cut them before they spread.

meditations.9.4.meaning: Whoever does wrong wrongs himself. Whoever acts unjustly harms himself, by making himself bad.
meditations.9.4.today: Wrongdoing damages the wrongdoer's character first, whatever it does to others.
meditations.9.4.you: Before cutting a corner, remember the first person it damages is you.

meditations.9.5.meaning: People often act unjustly by not doing something, not only by doing something.
meditations.9.5.today: Sins of omission count: silence when you should speak, inaction when you should help.
meditations.9.5.you: Is there something you're failing to do, a warning, a defence of someone, a decision, that is quietly unjust?

meditations.9.6.meaning: Present judgement based on understanding, present action aimed at the common good, and present contentment with whatever happens: that is enough.
meditations.9.6.today: Three conditions for a good moment, all achievable now, none depending on the future.
meditations.9.6.you: Check yourself right now: clear judgement, useful action, contentment. If all three, this moment is enough.

meditations.9.8.meaning: Animals share one life; rational beings share one intelligent soul, as we all share one earth, one light and one air.
meditations.9.8.today: Our shared reason connects us as surely as shared air.
meditations.9.8.you: When someone disagrees with you sharply, remember you share the same reason, as you share the same air.

meditations.9.9.meaning: Like things move towards like: earth to earth, water to water. Rational beings especially are drawn together, into friendships, families, communities and treaties. Only people have forgotten this attraction, yet nature still pulls them back.
meditations.9.9.today: Humans are built for connection, even when we drift apart. The pull back is natural.
meditations.9.9.you: If you've drifted from friends or family, trust the natural pull back. Reach out this month.

meditations.9.10.meaning: People, gods and the universe all bear fruit in season. We usually use the word for vines, but reason bears fruit too, for itself and for everyone.
meditations.9.10.today: Good thinking is productive: it yields better decisions, relationships and ideas.
meditations.9.10.you: What fruit did your reasoning bear this week, for your team or family? Name it.

meditations.9.13.meaning: Today I escaped all trouble, or rather I threw it out, because it wasn't outside me but in my opinions.
meditations.9.13.today: Trouble often lives in our interpretations, and we can throw it out.
meditations.9.13.you: End today by naming one trouble that was really an opinion, and throw it out.

meditations.9.14.meaning: Everything is the same: familiar in experience, brief in time, worthless in substance. Now is just like the time of those we buried.
meditations.9.14.today: Human life repeats. That's humbling, and it lightens the pressure of the present.
meditations.9.14.you: When today's crisis feels unique, remember how many similar ones those before you faced.

meditations.9.15.meaning: Things stand outside us, by themselves, knowing nothing and saying nothing about themselves. What judges them? Our ruling mind.
meditations.9.15.today: Events don't label themselves; we do. That's where our power lies.
meditations.9.15.you: Catch yourself labelling an event today as terrible or great. The label is yours, and optional.

meditations.9.16.meaning: Good and evil for a rational, social being lie not in what happens to it, but in what it does, just as its virtue and vice do.
meditations.9.16.today: Our character lives in our actions, not our circumstances.
meditations.9.16.you: On a bad day, remember your good lies in your actions, not in what happened to you.

meditations.9.17.meaning: For a stone thrown up, it's no evil to fall, and no good to have gone up.
meditations.9.17.today: Rises and falls in fortune are neither good nor bad in themselves.
meditations.9.17.you: Whether your career or project is rising or falling right now, treat it like the stone: neither is the point.

meditations.9.18.meaning: Look inside people's guiding principles and you'll see what kind of judges you're afraid of, and what kind of judges they are of themselves.
meditations.9.18.today: Fear of judgement often fades when we see the judges clearly.
meditations.9.18.you: Think of the person whose judgement you fear. How well do they judge themselves?

meditations.9.20.meaning: Your job is to leave another person's wrongdoing where it is.
meditations.9.20.today: We carry others' mistakes around with us. Leaving them where they happened is freeing.
meditations.9.20.you: Is there someone else's error you're still carrying? Put it down where it was made.

meditations.9.21.meaning: The end of an activity is a kind of death, and not an evil. Think of childhood, youth, adulthood and age: each change was a death. Were they terrible? So death itself isn't either.
meditations.9.21.today: We've already survived many endings: of childhood, of old jobs, of old selves.
meditations.9.21.you: List the versions of you that have already ended. None were tragedies. Neither is the next change.

meditations.9.22.meaning: Hurry to examine three minds: your own, to make it just; the universe's, to remember what you're part of; and your neighbour's, to know whether they acted from ignorance and to remember their mind is related to yours.
meditations.9.22.today: Self-examination, big-picture perspective and empathy: three checks for any situation.
meditations.9.22.you: In your next conflict, examine all three: your motives, the bigger picture, and the other person's understanding.

meditations.9.23.meaning: As you're part of a social system, let every act be part of social life. Any act not aimed at a social end breaks your life apart, like a person breaking from the consensus in an assembly.
meditations.9.23.today: Self-serving acts fragment us. Acts that serve others integrate us.
meditations.9.23.you: Check your week: which actions served no one but you? Could they be redirected?

meditations.9.24.meaning: Children's quarrels and games, poor souls carrying corpses around: that's everything. It makes the scenes of the underworld seem clearer.
meditations.9.24.today: From a distance, much adult seriousness looks like children's play.
meditations.9.24.you: When an argument at work gets heated, picture it as a children's squabble. Then respond like an adult.

meditations.9.25.meaning: Examine a thing's form, separated from its material, and consider it. Then work out the longest time something of that form can last.
meditations.9.25.today: Analysing essence and lifespan puts things in proportion.
meditations.9.25.you: Apply it to a current worry: what is it essentially, and how long will it realistically matter?

meditations.9.26.meaning: You've suffered endless trouble because you weren't content to let your mind do what it's made for. But enough of that.
meditations.9.26.today: Much suffering comes from resisting our own nature. The answer is simple: stop.
meditations.9.26.you: Where are you fighting your own best judgement? Enough. Let it lead.

meditations.9.27.meaning: When people blame or hate you, look into their souls and see what kind of people they are. You'll find no reason to worry about their opinion. Still, be kind to them; by nature they're friends, and the gods help them too.
meditations.9.27.today: Seeing critics clearly removes the sting, and kindness keeps your own character intact.
meditations.9.27.you: Next time you're criticised unfairly, look at the critic with understanding, then respond kindly anyway.

meditations.9.28.meaning: The universe cycles through the same patterns. Either an intelligence directs each event, and you should accept it; or it set things going once; or it's all atoms. In short, if there's a god, all is well; if chance, don't you be governed by chance.
meditations.9.28.today: Whatever your view of the cosmos, you can still govern yourself rationally.
meditations.9.28.you: Even if much of work feels random, you don't have to be. Act deliberately in your part of it.

meditations.9.30.meaning: Look down from above on the countless crowds of people, their ceremonies, voyages in storm and calm, births, lives and deaths. Think of past and future lives, and how many don't know your name or will soon forget it.
meditations.9.30.today: The overview effect: seeing humanity from above shrinks personal concerns.
meditations.9.30.you: When your name or reputation feels at stake, zoom out. Most of humanity will never know it, and that's fine.

meditations.9.31.meaning: Be undisturbed by what comes from outside, and be just in what comes from you: let your actions end in social good, as your nature requires.
meditations.9.31.today: Two rules: calm about external events, justice in your own actions.
meditations.9.31.you: Split your day's concerns into two columns: things that happened to me (stay calm) and things I do (act justly).

meditations.9.33.meaning: Everything you see will soon perish, and those who watched it perish will soon perish too. The one who dies very old ends up just like the one who died young.
meditations.9.33.today: Longevity doesn't change the destination. What matters is the journey.
meditations.9.33.you: Don't measure your life by length. Measure it by how you spend the days you have.

meditations.9.34.meaning: What are these people's guiding principles, what are they busy with, and why do they love and honour things? Imagine their souls laid bare. They think their blame harms and their praise helps. What an idea!
meditations.9.34.today: When we see people's motives clearly, their praise and blame lose power.
meditations.9.34.you: Picture the souls behind the loudest opinions about your work. Their verdicts matter less than you think.

meditations.9.36.meaning: How rotten the stuff of everything is: water, dust, bones, filth; marble is hardened earth, gold and silver are sediment, clothing is hair, purple dye is blood. Breath too changes from this to that.
meditations.9.36.today: De-glamourising valuable things weakens their hold on us.
meditations.9.36.you: Look at one status symbol you value and describe it in Marcus's plain terms. Notice its pull weaken.

meditations.9.37.meaning: Enough of this miserable life, grumbling and monkey tricks. What's disturbing you? Is it new? Look at its form, look at its matter; there's nothing else. Become simpler and better now. Examining it for a hundred years or three changes nothing.
meditations.9.37.today: Sometimes the right response to overthinking is: enough. Look plainly and act.
meditations.9.37.you: If you've been circling a problem for weeks, say enough, look at it plainly, and make the call.

meditations.9.38.meaning: If someone did wrong, the harm is theirs. But maybe they didn't do wrong.
meditations.9.38.today: Two corrections at once: wrongdoing harms the doer, and our accusations may be mistaken.
meditations.9.38.you: Before you decide someone wronged you, consider that they may not have.

meditations.9.39.meaning: Either everything comes from one intelligence and forms one body, and the part shouldn't complain about what serves the whole; or it's all atoms. Either way, why be disturbed? Ask your mind: are you dead, corrupted, pretending, turned beast?
meditations.9.39.today: Whatever the metaphysics, the practical check is the state of your own mind.
meditations.9.39.you: When disturbed, ask your mind Marcus's questions: am I corrupted, pretending or acting like a beast right now?

meditations.9.40.meaning: If the gods have power, pray not that bad things won't happen, but that you won't fear or desire or grieve over them. Instead of praying to keep something, pray not to fear losing it.
meditations.9.40.today: It redirects wishes from controlling outcomes to strengthening character.
meditations.9.40.you: If you pray or set intentions, try this: not for a result, but for the steadiness to meet any result.

meditations.9.41.meaning: Epicurus said that when ill, he didn't talk about his symptoms but kept discussing philosophy, keeping his mind free while his body suffered. Do the same in sickness and every other difficulty: don't abandon philosophy.
meditations.9.41.today: Keeping your mind on meaningful things during illness or hardship protects your wellbeing.
meditations.9.41.you: When you're unwell or under strain, keep a small daily practice going, even just this app.

meditations.10.2.meaning: Observe what your nature requires as a living thing, and accept it if it doesn't harm you as a living being. Then observe what you need as a rational, social being, and accept that too. Follow these rules and don't fuss about anything else.
meditations.10.2.today: Meeting basic needs, then rational and social ones, in order, is a sensible priority stack.
meditations.10.2.you: Check your basics first this week: sleep, food, movement. Then your thinking and relationships.

meditations.10.4.meaning: If someone's mistaken, teach them kindly and show their error. If you can't, blame yourself, or not even yourself.
meditations.10.4.today: Correction should be kind. And if it fails, don't pile on blame, even self-blame.
meditations.10.4.you: If a colleague doesn't take your correction, don't escalate or beat yourself up. Try again kindly later.

meditations.10.5.meaning: Whatever happens to you was prepared for you from all eternity; the web of causes has been spinning your thread and what comes with it since the beginning.
meditations.10.5.today: Seeing events as part of a long causal chain can reduce the sense of personal injustice.
meditations.10.5.you: When something unfair happens, see the long chain of causes behind it. It isn't aimed at you.

meditations.10.6.meaning: Whether atoms or ordered nature, I'm part of a whole, and related to others like me. So I won't resent anything the whole assigns me, and I'll aim my actions at the common good.
meditations.10.6.today: Belonging to a whole reduces resentment and orients action.
meditations.10.6.you: When your team or company hands you something unwelcome, remember you're part of the whole, and act for it.

meditations.10.7.meaning: The parts of the whole must change and perish. If that were bad for them, the whole couldn't be in good shape. So change isn't evil; it's how the whole renews itself.
meditations.10.7.today: In healthy systems, parts are replaced continuously. That's how the system lives.
meditations.10.7.you: You know systems need parts replaced to stay healthy. Apply that calmly to changes in your team and your life.

meditations.10.8.meaning: Once you've taken the names good, modest, truthful, rational, calm and generous, don't change them. If you lose them, return quickly. Rational means careful attention; calm means willing acceptance; generous means rising above pleasure, pain and fame.
meditations.10.8.today: Values are names you give yourself. Living up to them is the work.
meditations.10.8.you: Choose two of these names for yourself. When you slip, return to them quickly.

meditations.10.9.meaning: Farce, war, panic, lethargy and servitude will wipe out your principles day by day. Look and act so that your practical skill, your contemplation and your confidence all grow together.
meditations.10.9.today: Daily chaos erodes principles. Deliberate practice rebuilds them.
meditations.10.9.you: This daily practice is your defence against the erosion. Keep it going on chaotic days most of all.

meditations.10.10.meaning: A spider is proud of catching a fly; one man is proud of catching a hare, another fish, another boars, bears, or Sarmatians. Examine their principles: aren't they all robbers?
meditations.10.10.today: Marcus included his own military victories. Pride in conquest deserves suspicion.
meditations.10.10.you: Look at the wins you're proudest of. Were any of them captures rather than contributions?

meditations.10.12.meaning: Why suspicious fear, when you can simply ask what should be done? If you see clearly, go that way calmly. If not, pause and take the best advice. If obstacles arise, go on thoughtfully, holding to what seems just.
meditations.10.12.today: It's a clear decision procedure: inquire, act if clear, consult if not, persist justly.
meditations.10.12.you: Use it on your current decision: do you see clearly? If not, who are the best advisers to ask?

meditations.10.13.meaning: Ask yourself on waking: will it matter to me if someone else does what's right? It won't. And remember what those who give praise and blame so arrogantly are like at home, what they do and chase.
meditations.10.13.today: Others doing well costs you nothing. And arrogant judges are ordinary people up close.
meditations.10.13.you: Tomorrow morning, wish your rivals well. It costs you nothing.

meditations.10.14.meaning: The wise and modest person says to nature, which gives and takes back everything: give what you want, take back what you want. Not defiantly, but willingly and gladly.
meditations.10.14.today: Radical acceptance: open hands towards what life gives and takes.
meditations.10.14.you: Practise open hands with one thing this week, a plan or a possession, and see how it feels.

meditations.10.17.meaning: Always contemplate all of time and all of substance. Each individual thing is, in substance, a fig seed; in time, a turn of a drill.
meditations.10.17.today: Cosmic scale shrinks everyday dramas to their true size.
meditations.10.17.you: When something feels huge, picture it as a fig seed in all of substance. Then act proportionately.

meditations.10.18.meaning: Look at anything that exists and see that it's already dissolving and changing, decaying or dispersing, or made by nature to die.
meditations.10.18.today: Everything is already in the process of changing. Nothing is fixed.
meditations.10.18.you: Look at your current situation as already changing. It is. Plan accordingly.

meditations.10.19.meaning: Think what people are like when eating, sleeping, having sex or using the toilet. Then think of them being arrogant, angry or scolding from on high. Not long ago they were slaves to things, and soon they'll be gone.
meditations.10.19.today: Seeing powerful people as ordinary humans deflates intimidation.
meditations.10.19.you: Before meeting someone intimidating, picture them eating breakfast. It helps.

meditations.10.20.meaning: Whatever nature brings each thing is good for it, and good at the time it brings it.
meditations.10.20.today: Timing we didn't choose can still be the right timing.
meditations.10.20.you: Something arrived at an inconvenient time recently. Could its timing be right in a way you haven't seen?

meditations.10.21.meaning: The earth loves rain, the heavens love; the universe loves to make whatever will be. I tell the universe: I love what you love.
meditations.10.21.today: It's joyful acceptance: loving what the world is doing, not just enduring it.
meditations.10.21.you: Pick one change underway in your life and practise loving it as part of the world's making.

meditations.10.22.meaning: Either you live here and are used to it, or you leave by your own choice, or you die having done your duty. There's nothing else. So cheer up.
meditations.10.22.today: Three options, all acceptable. Anxiety has nowhere to land.
meditations.10.22.you: Apply it to a job or situation you're unsure about: stay contentedly, leave freely, or finish your duty. All fine.

meditations.10.23.meaning: This place is like any other. Everything here is the same as on a mountaintop or seashore. Living in a city can be like living in a shepherd's hut on a mountain, as Plato says.
meditations.10.23.today: Peace doesn't depend on location. You can find it where you are.
meditations.10.23.you: Stop waiting for the ideal holiday to feel calm. Find the mountain hut in your ordinary day.

meditations.10.24.meaning: What is my ruling mind to me right now? What am I making it? What am I using it for? Is it empty of understanding, cut off from others, melted into the body's cravings?
meditations.10.24.today: A quick mental health check: am I thinking clearly, connected and in control?
meditations.10.24.you: Ask these questions once today, perhaps mid-afternoon when energy dips.

meditations.10.25.meaning: Someone who runs from his master is a runaway. Law is our master, so whoever breaks it runs away. And whoever is grieved, angry or afraid about what the order of things has assigned is a runaway too.
meditations.10.25.today: Resentment of reality is a form of running away from it.
meditations.10.25.you: Where are you running from reality: through anger, fear or grief you haven't faced? Turn and face it.

meditations.10.26.meaning: A seed is planted and then another cause shapes it into a child; food is swallowed and another cause turns it into perception, motion and life. Look at these hidden powers and admire them, as we admire the invisible force of gravity.
meditations.10.26.today: Wonder at ordinary processes, conception, digestion, growth, is a healthy antidote to cynicism.
meditations.10.26.you: Watch your children or anything growing with fresh eyes this week. The hidden processes are astonishing.

meditations.10.27.meaning: Consider how everything now was the same before, and will be again. Picture whole dramas of the same shape: the courts of Hadrian, Antoninus, Philip, Alexander, Croesus. Only the actors change.
meditations.10.27.today: Institutional dramas repeat with new casts. Recognising the script helps you play your part wisely.
meditations.10.27.you: Name a recurring drama at work, a turf war or a reorganisation. You've seen this play before. How will you act this time?

meditations.10.28.meaning: Picture someone upset or discontented as a pig at the sacrifice, kicking and squealing. Or lying in bed silently lamenting our bonds. Only rational beings can follow events willingly; everyone must follow them.
meditations.10.28.today: Resistance doesn't change outcomes; it only adds suffering.
meditations.10.28.you: When you find yourself kicking against the inevitable, remember the pig. Choose to walk instead.

meditations.10.29.meaning: With each thing you do, pause and ask: is death terrible because it takes this away?
meditations.10.29.today: It's a test of what's truly valuable: would losing it to death matter?
meditations.10.29.you: Ask it of your screen time this week. Would death depriving you of it be a loss?

meditations.10.31.meaning: When you see one person, think of someone like them from the past; when you look at yourself, think of any other Caesar. Where are they now? Nowhere. Everything human is smoke. What remains is to live well your brief portion.
meditations.10.31.today: Every type has had a predecessor who's now gone. It humbles and clarifies.
meditations.10.31.you: When you look at yourself in your role, think of whoever held it before you. Live your turn well.

meditations.10.32.meaning: Let no one truthfully say you aren't simple or good. Make anyone who says so a liar. That's entirely in your power: who can stop you being good and simple? Decide not to live unless you are.
meditations.10.32.today: Your character is the one reputation fully in your control.
meditations.10.32.you: Make it your goal this week that no one could truthfully call you anything but simple and good.

meditations.10.34.meaning: For someone who's absorbed true principles, even a line of poetry is enough to banish grief and fear: leaves, some the wind scatters, so are the generations of people. Your children are leaves; praisers and critics are leaves; all fall and grow again.
meditations.10.34.today: One line remembered at the right moment can reset a whole mood.
meditations.10.34.you: Keep one short line from this practice in your pocket for hard moments. Leaves is a good one.

meditations.10.35.meaning: A healthy eye sees everything and doesn't demand only green things. A healthy stomach digests all food. A healthy mind should be ready for everything that happens, not demand that children live or everyone praise it.
meditations.10.35.today: Resilience means accepting the full range of experience rather than insisting on only the pleasant.
meditations.10.35.you: Where are you demanding only the green things, praise, easy days? Practise welcoming the rest.

meditations.10.36.meaning: No one is so lucky that no one at their deathbed is glad to see them go. Even a good man will hear someone thinking, finally relieved of that schoolmaster. So leave calmly, without clinging; people's relief shouldn't make you resent them.
meditations.10.36.today: Not everyone will mourn us, and that's human. It shouldn't embitter us.
meditations.10.36.you: Some people may be relieved when you move on from a role. Let that free you rather than hurt you.

meditations.10.37.meaning: Whenever someone does something, get into the habit of asking: what's their aim? But start with yourself, and examine yourself first.
meditations.10.37.today: Understanding motives, starting with your own, improves judgement and reduces conflict.
meditations.10.37.you: Before assuming someone's motive in a decision, ask what your own motive is.

meditations.11.2.meaning: You'll value songs, dances and wrestling bouts less if you break them into single notes and moves and ask whether each one masters you. You'll be ashamed to say yes. Do this with everything except virtue: break it into parts and it loses its hold.
meditations.11.2.today: Breaking a compulsion into small pieces weakens it. It works for binge-watching, scrolling and shopping.
meditations.11.2.you: Break a habit you can't resist, like a feed, into its individual swipes. Does any single swipe deserve your attention?

meditations.11.3.meaning: How admirable is a soul ready to leave the body at any moment, whether that means extinction, scattering or continuing, as long as the readiness comes from its own judgement, calmly and with dignity, not from mere stubbornness or theatrical display.
meditations.11.3.today: Marcus contrasts reasoned calm about death with defiant displays. The point is thoughtful readiness, not bravado.
meditations.11.3.you: Make peace with endings through reflection rather than bravado. Calm readiness beats dramatic defiance.

meditations.11.5.meaning: What's your craft? Being good. And how is it done well, except through principles about the nature of the universe and of human beings?
meditations.11.5.today: Goodness is a skill with underlying knowledge, like engineering or medicine.
meditations.11.5.you: Treat being good as your core craft, one you study and practise daily, alongside your professional one.

meditations.11.6.meaning: Tragedy was invented to remind people what happens in life and that it's natural, so we can bear on life's larger stage what we watch in the theatre. Then comedy mocked vanity; later forms drifted into mere cleverness.
meditations.11.6.today: Stories help us rehearse hardship. Good drama prepares us; mere entertainment distracts.
meditations.11.6.you: Choose stories that prepare you for life rather than ones that simply distract. It's a better use of screen time.

meditations.11.7.meaning: How obvious it is that no situation is better suited to practising philosophy than the one you're in right now.
meditations.11.7.today: We wait for ideal conditions to grow. The best conditions are the current ones.
meditations.11.7.you: Your busy job and full family life aren't obstacles to practice. They're the exact place for it.

meditations.11.8.meaning: A branch cut from its neighbour is cut from the whole tree. A person cut off from another cuts himself off from the whole community, and does it himself, through hatred. But nature lets us graft back on, though repeated breaks make reunion harder.
meditations.11.8.today: Estrangement can be repaired, but each break makes the next repair harder.
meditations.11.8.you: Is there a relationship you've let break? Graft it back soon, before it becomes harder.

meditations.11.9.meaning: Those who block your right action can't turn you aside from it, so don't let them turn you from goodwill towards them either. Guard both: steady action and gentleness towards those who obstruct you.
meditations.11.9.today: Staying firm on substance while staying kind in manner is a rare leadership skill.
meditations.11.9.you: In your next standoff, hold your position firmly and your tone gently. Both at once.

meditations.11.10.meaning: Nature is never inferior to art, since art imitates nature. The most perfect nature can't fall short of art's skill. Art makes lesser things serve greater ones, and so does nature; that's where justice comes from.
meditations.11.10.today: Good design copies nature's logic: parts serving the whole. Justice follows from that order.
meditations.11.10.you: Anyone who designs systems copies nature's structure. Apply the same logic to fairness in how you lead.

meditations.11.11.meaning: The things you chase and flee don't come to you; you go to them. Let your judgement about them rest, and they'll stay still, and you won't be seen chasing or fleeing.
meditations.11.11.today: Much agitation is self-generated pursuit. Stop the pursuit and the agitation settles.
meditations.11.11.you: What are you chasing that isn't chasing you? Let the judgement rest, and see if it quietens.

meditations.11.12.meaning: The soul keeps its sphere-like shape when it isn't stretched towards things, shrunk inwards, scattered or sunk, but lit from within, seeing the truth about everything and about itself.
meditations.11.12.today: A balanced mind is neither grasping, withdrawn nor scattered, but clear and self-aware.
meditations.11.12.you: Check your mind today: grasping, shrinking, scattered or clear? Aim for the sphere.

meditations.11.14.meaning: People despise and flatter each other; they want to rise above each other and grovel before each other.
meditations.11.14.today: Status games of contempt and flattery are ancient and everywhere.
meditations.11.14.you: Notice the despise-and-flatter game in your organisation. Step out of both halves of it.

meditations.11.15.meaning: How insincere it is to announce, I'm going to be straight with you. Why say it? It shows in your actions. Character is written on the face and in the eyes. The honest, good person is like someone who smells: you notice them the moment they walk in.
meditations.11.15.today: Announcing honesty often signals the opposite. Real integrity is obvious without a preface.
meditations.11.15.you: Drop phrases like to be honest or I'll be frank. Let your conduct make them unnecessary.

meditations.11.16.meaning: The power to live well is in the soul, if it stays indifferent to what doesn't matter. It will, if it looks at each thing separately and together, remembering that things don't form opinions about themselves; we do.
meditations.11.16.today: Indifference to trivia is not apathy; it's clear prioritisation.
meditations.11.16.you: Pick three things you're currently fretting about and ask whether they truly matter. Let go of those that don't.

meditations.11.17.meaning: Consider where each thing came from, what it's made of, what it's turning into, what it will be after, and that it will suffer no harm.
meditations.11.17.today: A five-step lens that makes change feel natural rather than threatening.
meditations.11.17.you: Apply the five steps to a change you're anxious about. Notice that transformation isn't harm.

meditations.11.19.meaning: Guard against four faults of the mind and wipe them out when you spot them: this thought is unnecessary; this undermines community; this isn't what you really think; and this comes from letting the lower self defeat the divine part in you.
meditations.11.19.today: It's a four-point filter for thoughts and words: necessary, cooperative, sincere, self-controlled.
meditations.11.19.you: Run your next difficult email through the four filters before sending it.

meditations.11.20.meaning: Your fiery and airy elements naturally rise, and your earthy and watery ones sink, yet all obey the arrangement of the whole and stay where they're placed. Only your mind rebels against its place. Resentment and anger are that rebellion.
meditations.11.20.today: Everything else accepts its role in the system; only we resist ours through resentment.
meditations.11.20.you: When resentment rises about your role or situation, remember even the elements accept their place.

meditations.11.22.meaning: Think of the country mouse and the town mouse, and the town mouse's alarm and panic.
meditations.11.22.today: Aesop's fable: the rich, anxious life versus the simple, calm one.
meditations.11.22.you: Are you living as the town mouse, surrounded by plenty but anxious? What would a country-mouse week look like?

meditations.11.23.meaning: Socrates called the opinions of the crowd bogeymen, the monsters used to frighten children.
meditations.11.23.today: Public opinion often frightens us more than it should, like a childhood monster.
meditations.11.23.you: Which imagined crowd opinion is stopping you from doing something right? Treat it as a bogeyman.

meditations.11.24.meaning: At public shows, the Spartans put seats in the shade for strangers and sat anywhere themselves.
meditations.11.24.today: True hospitality puts guests first, and true status doesn't need the best seat.
meditations.11.24.you: In meetings and at home, give others the best seat, the time slot or the credit.

meditations.11.25.meaning: Socrates declined an invitation from King Perdiccas, saying he didn't want to die the worst death: receiving favours he couldn't repay.
meditations.11.25.today: Accepting favours from the powerful can create obligations that compromise us.
meditations.11.25.you: Be careful with favours from people whose goodwill might later come with strings.

meditations.11.26.meaning: The Ephesians had a precept: always keep in mind someone from the past who practised virtue.
meditations.11.26.today: Role models, kept in mind, pull us towards better behaviour.
meditations.11.26.you: Choose one person, historic or personal, to keep in mind this week as your model.

meditations.11.27.meaning: The Pythagoreans said to look at the sky each morning, to remember the stars that do the same work the same way, and their purity and nakedness. There's no veil over a star.
meditations.11.27.today: A morning glance at the sky is a reminder of steadiness, transparency and purpose.
meditations.11.27.you: Replace the first glance at your phone with a glance at the sky tomorrow morning.

meditations.11.28.meaning: Picture Socrates wrapping himself in an animal skin after Xanthippe went out with his cloak, and what he said to friends embarrassed to be seen with him.
meditations.11.28.today: Socrates didn't care about looking foolish. His ease with embarrassment was a kind of freedom.
meditations.11.28.you: Next time you feel embarrassed by something trivial, think of Socrates in his skin, unbothered.

meditations.11.33.meaning: Looking for figs in winter is madness. So is looking for your child when that's no longer allowed.
meditations.11.33.today: Grieving what's gone is natural; demanding it back is not. It's a hard teaching from a father who lost many children.
meditations.11.33.you: Treasure your children now, in their season, knowing seasons change.

meditations.11.34.meaning: Epictetus said: when you kiss your child, whisper, tomorrow you may die. Ill-omened? No word describing nature's work is ill-omened, or talking about harvesting corn would be too.
meditations.11.34.today: Remembering mortality at tender moments makes them more precious, not less.
meditations.11.34.you: Tonight, when you say goodnight to your children, hold the moment a little longer, knowing it's fleeting.

meditations.11.35.meaning: Unripe grape, ripe bunch, raisin: all changes, not into nothing, but into something not yet existing.
meditations.11.35.today: Each stage of life is a transformation, not a loss.
meditations.11.35.you: Whichever stage your career or family is in, it's turning into something new, not nothing.

meditations.11.38.meaning: Epictetus said the dispute isn't about some ordinary matter, but about whether we're sane or mad.
meditations.11.38.today: Some disagreements are really about basic sanity: whether we're thinking clearly at all.
meditations.11.38.you: When a debate escalates, ask whether you're still thinking clearly. That's often the real question.

meditations.11.39.meaning: Socrates asked: what do you want, rational souls or irrational? Rational. Healthy or unhealthy? Healthy. Why not seek them then? We have them. Then why fight and quarrel?
meditations.11.39.today: If we believe we're reasonable, our quarrels are hard to justify.
meditations.11.39.you: Next time you're in a quarrel, ask Socrates' question: if we're both reasonable, why are we fighting?

meditations.12.2.meaning: God sees people's minds stripped of the body and its impurities. If you train yourself to look at people that way too, you'll spare yourself a lot of trouble about appearances, clothing, reputation and status.
meditations.12.2.today: Looking past surface markers to the person's mind reduces both prejudice and envy.
meditations.12.2.you: In your next meeting, try to see past title and appearance to how each person thinks.

meditations.12.3.meaning: You're made of three things: a little body, a little breath and a mind. The first two are yours to look after; only the mind is truly yours. Separate from yourself what others do and say, your own past, future worries and bodily sensations, and you'll live the present in peace.
meditations.12.3.today: Distinguishing what's truly yours from what isn't is the core of emotional freedom.
meditations.12.3.you: When stressed, list what's actually yours in the situation. Look after the body; own only the mind.

meditations.12.4.meaning: I often wonder how everyone loves themselves more than anyone else, yet values others' opinions of them more than their own. If told to think nothing they wouldn't say aloud, they couldn't manage a single day.
meditations.12.4.today: We care more about others' views of us than our own, a paradox social media magnifies.
meditations.12.4.you: Give your own judgement of yourself more weight this week than anyone else's.

meditations.12.5.meaning: How could the gods, who arranged everything well, have allowed good people to be extinguished at death? But if that's how it is, trust that it was right, since it would otherwise have been arranged differently.
meditations.12.5.today: Marcus wrestles honestly with a hard question about death and justice, and lands on trust.
meditations.12.5.you: When you face a question without an answer, it's fine to leave it open and trust, as Marcus did.

meditations.12.6.meaning: Practise even what you despair of doing well. The left hand, useless for most things, holds the reins better than the right because it's practised at that.
meditations.12.6.today: Skill is built by practice, not talent, even in areas we feel weak.
meditations.12.6.you: Pick one weak skill, perhaps public speaking or patience, and practise it deliberately this month.

meditations.12.7.meaning: Consider what state of body and soul you should be in when death arrives; how short life is, how vast the gulf of time before and after, and how frail all matter.
meditations.12.7.today: Picturing the state you'd want to be in at the end clarifies how to live now.
meditations.12.7.you: Describe how you'd like to be, in character, when your time comes. Live towards that.

meditations.12.8.meaning: Look at the forms of things stripped bare, at the purposes of actions, at what pain, pleasure, death and fame are. See who causes their own distress, that no one is really hindered by another, and that everything is opinion.
meditations.12.8.today: A compressed review of Stoic analysis tools: essence, purpose, and the role of opinion.
meditations.12.8.you: Use it as a weekly review: what's the real purpose of what I did, and where did opinion cause my distress?

meditations.12.9.meaning: Use your principles like a boxer, not a gladiator. The gladiator can drop his sword and be killed; the boxer always has his fists and only has to use them.
meditations.12.9.today: Principles should be part of you, not a tool you can drop under pressure.
meditations.12.9.you: Make your principles like fists, always there, rather than a sword you might drop in a crisis.

meditations.12.10.meaning: See what things are in themselves, splitting them into matter, form and purpose.
meditations.12.10.today: It's first-principles analysis in one line: what's it made of, what shape, what for?
meditations.12.10.you: Apply it to a new project or tool: its material, its form and its real purpose.

meditations.12.11.meaning: What power humans have: to do only what God would approve, and to accept whatever God gives.
meditations.12.11.today: We have two powers always available: right action and acceptance.
meditations.12.11.you: Use both today: act only in ways you'd be proud of, and accept what you can't change.

meditations.12.12.meaning: For what happens naturally, blame neither gods, who do no wrong, nor people, who only do wrong unwillingly. So blame no one.
meditations.12.12.today: Blame rarely helps anyone improve. Understanding and calm correction almost always do more good.
meditations.12.12.you: Try a day of blaming no one, including yourself. Fix things instead.

meditations.12.13.meaning: How ridiculous, and what a stranger to the world, is someone who's surprised by anything that happens in life.
meditations.12.13.today: Surprise at ordinary misfortune signals unfamiliarity with how life works.
meditations.12.13.you: Before reacting to bad news, remind yourself it's the kind of thing life produces. No surprise needed.

meditations.12.14.meaning: Either there's fixed necessity, or a kind providence, or aimless chaos. If necessity, why resist? If providence, make yourself worthy of its help. If chaos, be glad you have a guiding mind of your own in the storm.
meditations.12.14.today: Three worldviews, one practical response: act well and stay steady.
meditations.12.14.you: Whatever you believe about fate, the response is the same: steer your own ship well.

meditations.12.15.meaning: A lamp shines undimmed until it goes out. Will the truth, justice and self-control in you go out before you do?
meditations.12.15.today: Character can fade before life ends, if we let it.
meditations.12.15.you: Keep your lamp lit: protect your honesty and self-control from slow erosion.

meditations.12.16.meaning: When someone seems to have done wrong, ask: how do I know it's wrong? And even if it is, maybe they've already condemned themselves. Wanting bad people not to do wrong is like wanting figs without juice or babies not to cry.
meditations.12.16.today: Judgement of others should be slow, and our expectations of them realistic rather than ideal.
meditations.12.16.you: When you're quick to condemn a colleague, slow down: are you sure, and might they already regret it?

meditations.12.18.meaning: With anything that makes an impression on you, look at what it is, and analyse it into form, matter, purpose and the time in which it must end.
meditations.12.18.today: Breaking an impression into its parts is a structured analysis that defuses impulsive reactions.
meditations.12.18.you: Before reacting to a provocative message, break it down: what's it made of, what's it for, how long will it matter?

meditations.12.20.meaning: First, do nothing thoughtlessly or without a purpose. Second, aim your actions only at a social good.
meditations.12.20.today: Two simple rules cover most of life: be deliberate in what you do, and do it to serve others.
meditations.12.20.you: Use them as a filter for tomorrow's calendar: is each item deliberate, and does it serve others?

meditations.12.21.meaning: Soon you'll be nobody and nowhere, and so will everything and everyone you see now. All things are made to change and perish so that other things can follow.
meditations.12.21.today: Impermanence makes room for renewal. That's the design, not a flaw.
meditations.12.21.you: Let this ease your grip on any role or status. Your turn will pass so others can have theirs.

meditations.12.23.meaning: An activity that ends at its proper time suffers no harm by ending. So neither does a life, which is a series of acts, when it ends at its time. Nature sets the time, and what serves the whole is good.
meditations.12.23.today: Endings at their time are completions, not failures.
meditations.12.23.you: When a project or phase ends, treat it as completed rather than cut short.

meditations.12.24.meaning: Keep three principles ready: act only as justice would, and don't blame chance or providence for what comes from outside; remember what each being is from seed to death; and see human affairs from above, so you'll scorn what's small.
meditations.12.24.today: Justice, perspective on life's arc, and the view from above: three steady tools.
meditations.12.24.you: Carry these three into your next hard week: act justly, remember life's arc, look from above.

meditations.12.26.meaning: When you're troubled, you've forgotten that everything follows nature; that others' wrongs aren't yours; that everything has always happened this way; how close your kinship is with all people; that everyone's mind is divine; that nothing is truly ours; that everything is opinion; and that we live only now.
meditations.12.26.today: Most distress is forgetting. This list is a reminder of everything we forget when upset.
meditations.12.26.you: Save this list for your worst moments. Read it through once before reacting.

meditations.12.27.meaning: Recall people who complained bitterly, or were famous for fame, disaster, enmity or fortune. Where are they now? Smoke, ashes and a story, or not even a story. So what's worth our effort?
meditations.12.27.today: Great passions and famous feuds end as smoke. Perspective helps us choose what to care about.
meditations.12.27.you: Think of a feud or grievance you're nursing. In time, it will be smoke. Let go sooner.

meditations.12.28.meaning: To those who ask where he's seen the gods: first, they can be seen; second, he's never seen his own soul yet honours it. He knows the gods by experiencing their power.
meditations.12.28.today: Some realities are known by their effects, not by direct sight.
meditations.12.28.you: Trust the effects you see of good practices, like this daily one, even when the mechanism isn't visible.

meditations.12.29.meaning: The safety of life is to examine everything thoroughly, its material and form, to act justly with all your soul and speak the truth. What remains but to enjoy life, linking one good act to the next without gaps?
meditations.12.29.today: A good life as a chain of good acts, joined so closely there's no room for anything else.
meditations.12.29.you: Try linking good acts back to back tomorrow, one after another, leaving little room for pettiness.

meditations.12.30.meaning: There's one sunlight, though split by walls and mountains; one substance, though spread among countless bodies; one soul, one intelligent mind, though it seems divided. Only intelligent things are drawn to their own kind and feel fellowship.
meditations.12.30.today: Underneath division, we share one light and one reason.
meditations.12.30.you: When people seem divided at work or at home, look for the one light shining through all of them.

meditations.12.31.meaning: What do you want? To go on existing, sensing, moving, growing, speaking, thinking? If these seem of little value, turn to what remains: following reason and God. It's inconsistent to honour those and be troubled that death will take the rest.
meditations.12.31.today: If we value reason above everything, we can face losing the rest calmly.
meditations.12.31.you: List what you want most from life. If reason and goodness are at the top, death loses much of its sting.

meditations.12.32.meaning: How small a share of infinite time each person gets, how small a portion of substance, of the universal soul, of the earth you crawl on. Think nothing great except acting as your nature leads and bearing what nature brings.
meditations.12.32.today: Cosmic smallness focuses us on the two things that matter: acting well and bearing well.
meditations.12.32.you: When something feels overwhelmingly important, remember your small clod of earth, then act and bear well.

meditations.12.33.meaning: How does the ruling mind use itself? That's everything. All else, in your power or not, is lifeless ash and smoke.
meditations.12.33.today: How you use your mind is the whole game. Everything else is secondary.
meditations.12.33.you: End today by asking one question: how did I use my mind today? That's the scorecard.

meditations.12.34.meaning: The most useful reflection for scorning death: even people who think pleasure good and pain evil have despised it.
meditations.12.34.today: If even pleasure-lovers face death calmly, so can we.
meditations.12.34.you: Let the courage of others, even those who disagree with you, strengthen your own calm.

meditations.12.35.meaning: For someone to whom only what comes in its season is good, who doesn't care whether they did more or fewer right acts, or watched the world for a longer or shorter time, death isn't frightening.
meditations.12.35.today: Quality over quantity removes the fear of running out of time.
meditations.12.35.you: Measure your life by the quality of your acts, not their number. Then time loses its terror.

meditations.1.1.meaning: Marcus opens his private notebook by crediting his grandfather with two things: basic decency and control of his temper. He doesn't say he was born calm. He says he learned it by watching someone. Temper, in this view, is a skill passed from person to person, not a fixed trait.
meditations.1.1.today: Psychologists call this modelling: children, teams and whole organisations copy the emotional tone of whoever is in charge. A manager who stays level in a crisis quietly trains everyone around them to do the same.
meditations.1.1.you: You are someone's grandfather Verus right now, at work and at home. When a test fails or a system misbehaves, your team learns how to react by watching you. So do your family, when a plan falls apart at home.

meditations.1.5.meaning: From his childhood tutor Marcus took a short list of unglamorous habits: don't join a fan club, put up with hard work, want little, do your own work, stay out of other people's business, and refuse to listen to gossip. It's a portrait of a self-contained person.
meditations.1.5.today: Swap chariot teams for politics, sport or online pile-ons and the advice lands exactly. Tribes form fast on social media, and gossip travels further than ever. Doing your own work and ignoring the noise is now a competitive advantage.
meditations.1.5.you: Replacing Instagram is this passage in action: stepping out of the arena of fans and factions. At work, notice which internal factions pull you in, and where you could simply do the work with your own hands instead.

meditations.1.6.meaning: Diognetus taught the boy Marcus to ignore trivia and quackery, not to get hooked on hobbies like quail-fighting, to accept blunt criticism, and to take philosophy seriously enough to live more simply. In short: aim your enthusiasm at things that matter.
meditations.1.6.today: Every era has its quail fights: fantasy leagues, doom-scrolling, the latest miracle product. They aren't evil, but they soak up the passion you could spend on work, people or learning. Frank feedback is also rarer than ever, and more valuable.
meditations.1.6.you: Ask where your passion goes each week. If you build systems for a living, you'll be pitched miracle cures constantly: tools and methods that promise everything. Diognetus would say listen to the plain truth-tellers and ignore the miracle-sellers.

meditations.1.7.meaning: Rusticus told young Marcus, in effect, you need work. Then he taught him not to show off with clever talk or public displays of virtue, to write plainly, to make peace quickly with people who'd wronged him, and to read carefully. He also handed him Epictetus, which changed Marcus's life.
meditations.1.7.today: Performed virtue is everywhere now: posting about good deeds, polished thought-leadership. Rusticus's test still works. Do the good thing quietly, write clearly, forgive fast, and read the real book rather than the summary.
meditations.1.7.you: Who in your life is your Rusticus, the person who tells you plainly where you fall short? Keep them close. And when you write to your team, choose plain words over impressive ones.

meditations.1.8.meaning: Apollonius showed Marcus a man who was steady whatever happened, in pain, grief or long illness, and who could be firm and flexible at once. He also taught how to accept favours gracefully: neither embarrassed by them nor taking them for granted.
meditations.1.8.today: We tend to think steadiness means stiffness. Apollonius shows the opposite: a steady person bends where it's wise and holds where it matters. And accepting help well is a skill most high performers never learn.
meditations.1.8.you: When pressure spikes, a launch slips or a hard family moment arrives, aim for the same you as on an ordinary Tuesday. And when a colleague or someone at home does you a favour, receive it warmly instead of waving it away.

meditations.1.9.meaning: Sextus was warm but dignified, took friends' interests seriously, and was patient with people who hadn't thought things through. Everyone liked being around him, yet everyone respected him. Marcus admires that rare mix of affection without flattery and seriousness without coldness.
meditations.1.9.today: Many leaders pick one: liked or respected. Sextus shows you can be both, by being genuinely interested in others while keeping your standards. Patience with uninformed opinions is especially useful in an age of instant takes.
meditations.1.9.you: Picture the colleague who forms opinions about your systems without reading the details. Sextus would be patient with them without pretending they're right. At home, it means warmth that doesn't give up on standards.

meditations.1.13.meaning: From Catulus: when a friend criticises you, even unfairly, don't shrug it off; help them back to their usual good self. Speak well of your teachers. Love your children for real. Three short lessons about loyalty.
meditations.1.13.today: Most of us either get defensive or cut people off when criticised. Catulus suggests a third path: treat the criticism as a sign something's off with the relationship and repair it. Gratitude to teachers and real warmth at home never go out of date.
meditations.1.13.you: Is there a colleague or family member whose recent criticism you've dismissed? Try one repair conversation this week. And name a mentor you owe something to, out loud, to someone.

meditations.1.15.meaning: Maximus was self-governed and cheerful even when ill. He meant what he said, did what was in front of him without complaining, and was never rushed, never procrastinating, never sulking, never faking a laugh to hide irritation. Marcus lists these nevers as a target.
meditations.1.15.today: Burnout culture swings between frantic hurry and avoidance. Maximus models a third speed: unhurried but prompt. His honesty about irritation, no fake laughs, is also healthier than the forced positivity many workplaces run on.
meditations.1.15.you: Pick one never for this week: never in a hurry, never putting off, or never masking annoyance with a joke. Try it in meetings and at dinner. Notice which is hardest for you.

meditations.1.16.meaning: The long portrait of Antoninus Pius, the adoptive father who trained Marcus to rule, is really a leadership manual. Be mild but decisive, stay indifferent to honours, work hard, listen to anyone with a good idea, reward fairly, plan ahead, and don't chase popularity.
meditations.1.16.today: Swap emperor for CEO, general or head of department and almost every line still applies. Particularly modern: listening to anyone with something useful to propose, regardless of rank, which is exactly what good engineering and military cultures try to build.
meditations.1.16.you: Read this as a checklist for how you lead your teams. Which trait would your team say you already have? Which one would they quietly wish you had? Choose that one to practise.

meditations.1.17.meaning: Marcus ends Book 1 by thanking the gods for everything that went right: family, teachers, friends, even temptations he was never exposed to. His point is humility. Most of what made him good came from outside him, including sheer luck.
meditations.1.17.today: Research on gratitude links it to wellbeing, but Marcus's version is sharper. It's an honest audit of what you didn't earn. Successful people easily forget the luck and help behind them, and that forgetting breeds arrogance.
meditations.1.17.you: Write your own short Book 1: the people who formed you, and the luck you had. It's a good antidote on days when your work or position makes you feel self-made.

meditations.2.1.meaning: Each morning Marcus reminded himself: today I'll meet difficult people, meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, dishonest. They act this way because they don't know better. They can't really hurt me, and I can't hate them, because we're made to work together like two hands.
meditations.2.1.today: This is a pre-game briefing for the day. Expecting friction removes the shock of it, and seeing others as ignorant rather than evil makes it easier to cooperate. Crisis teams and pilots rehearse problems before they happen for exactly this reason.
meditations.2.1.you: This could be your Pre-Game Shield in its oldest form. Before work, name the one or two people likely to test you today, and decide in advance to treat them as partners on the same mission.

meditations.5.1.meaning: The emperor admits he'd rather stay in bed. Then he argues himself up: plants, birds and bees all do their jobs, so why won't you do yours? Rest has limits, and you overdo comfort while underdoing effort. If you loved your own nature, you'd love its work.
meditations.5.1.today: Every morning is a small negotiation with the snooze button and the phone. Marcus's move is to connect getting up with purpose, not willpower: I'm rising to do the work of a human being.
meditations.5.1.you: Tomorrow, before you pick up your phone, finish this sentence: today I'm getting up to... Make it about the people you serve or build for, not the inbox.

meditations.2.5.meaning: Do each thing with full attention and simple dignity, fairly and warmly, as though it were the last thing you'll ever do. That clears away carelessness, pretence and self-pity, and life starts to flow quietly.
meditations.2.5.today: This is deep work, two thousand years early. Multitasking fractures attention, and treating each task as your last forces you to be fully present. It works for a code review, a conversation or bedtime with a child.
meditations.2.5.you: Choose one task tomorrow, perhaps a design review or a one-to-one, and give it your whole attention, phone out of sight. Then do the same for one conversation at home.

meditations.2.4.meaning: Marcus scolds himself: you've been putting this off for years, and you've had chance after chance. Your time is limited. If you don't use it to clear your mind, it will be gone, and so will you.
meditations.2.4.today: Procrastination is rarely laziness; it's avoiding discomfort. Marcus answers with mortality: the window is finite. Deadline research agrees that a real, felt limit is what moves us.
meditations.2.4.you: Name the thing you've been meaning to change for years, a habit, a conversation, a project. What's one step you could take this week, while the window is open?

meditations.3.4.meaning: Stop spending your life wondering what other people are doing, saying, thinking or plotting, unless it serves a real common good. It pulls you away from managing your own mind. Only think thoughts you'd be comfortable saying out loud.
meditations.3.4.today: Social media is a machine for wondering about other people. Workplace politics runs on the same fuel. Marcus's test, would I be happy to reveal what I'm thinking right now, is a powerful filter for mental clutter.
meditations.3.4.you: Notice how much of your day goes on speculating about a colleague, a rival team or someone's motives. Each time, redirect to the question Marcus would ask: what's my next useful action?

meditations.4.2.meaning: One line: don't do anything without a purpose, and do everything according to the best rules of the craft. Marcus thinks of life as a craft with standards, like carpentry.
